content: Dr. Hala Sakr, representing the WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean, contributed her expertise to the initiative. Dr. Manfred Huber, from the WHO Regional Office for Europe, also participated in the effort. Dr. Patanjali Nayar, affiliated with the WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia, provided his professional input. Mr. Darryl Barret and Ms. Pauline Kleinitz, both from the WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific, were involved in the project. Dr. Vivath Chou, a Technical Officer for Disability and Rehabilitation at the WHO Representative Office in Cambodia, played a role in the discussions. Mr. Satish Mishra, from the WHO Representative Office in Tajikistan, also contributed to the work. Dr. Viola Artikova, an independent international consultant on disability based in the United States, provided her insights. Dr. Luis Guillermo Ibarra, Director of the WHO Collaborating Center for Research and Medical Rehabilitation at the National Institute of Rehabilitation in Mexico City, Mexico, participated in the initiative. Dr. Mohamed Khalil Diouri, Head of Rehabilitation Services and Geriatrics at the Directorate of Population, Ministry of Health in Rabat, Morocco, shared his expertise. Associate Professor Sergey Maltsev, Deputy Director and Head of the Department of Rehabilitation at the St. Petersburg Medico-Social Institute under the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection in the Russian Federation, contributed to the discussions. Mrs. Cecilia Nleya, Deputy Director of Rehabilitation Services at the Ministry of Health and Child Care in Harare, Zimbabwe, was also involved. Dr. Rajendra Prasad, a Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon and Spine Surgeon at Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals in Delhi, India, provided his professional input. Dr. Alaa Sebah, an independent international consultant on disability and child protection from Egypt, participated in the initiative. Dr. Pratima Singh, a consultant in rehabilitation medicine at the Ministry of Health and Medical Sciences in Suva, Fiji, contributed her expertise. Dr. Carlos Quintero Valencia, a rehabilitation medicine specialist at Antioquia University in Medellín, Colombia, was also part of the discussions. All members of the Guideline Development Group completed WHO declaration of interest forms. These forms were reviewed by the Secretariat to assess any potential conflicts of interest and determine whether participation was appropriate or if adjustments to the nature of their involvement were necessary. Three members declared potential conflicts of interest related to research support. Dr. Christoph Gutenbrunner disclosed involvement with German Pension Insurance research projects, which had no monetary value. Dr. Gwynneth Llewellyn declared an income of AUD 185,000 in 2011 for her work in disability research and her involvement in drafting a position paper on the health rehabilitation workforce in the Pacific. Dr. Vibha Krishnamurthy disclosed a research grant to the Ummeed Child Development Center for developing an international guide to monitor and support child development. Dr. Lynne Turner-Stokes declared a potential conflict of interest due to her roles as a consultant physician in rehabilitation medicine and as Director of the Regional Rehabilitation Unit at King’s College London. Similarly, Dr. Frances Simmonds disclosed her position as Director of the Australian Rehabilitation Outcomes Centre and noted that her university held intellectual property rights to a case-mix classification system (AN-SNAP). None of these declarations were deemed to exclude participation in the Guideline Development Group or to require amendments to the nature of their involvement.
